name: Axion
tagline: Small embeddable pure-Java SQL database with a JDBC driver, from the early-2000s Tigris.org community.
description: Axion is an open-source relational database engine written in and for Java, developed from 2002 on Tigris.org by a group that included Rodney Waldhoff, James Strachan and Geir Magnusson Jr. Applications embed it through a JDBC driver and choose in-memory or disk-backed databases and tables; it parses SQL with a JavaCC grammar, supports B-tree and array indexes, sequences, constraints and snapshot-isolation transactions. Its niche was the same as HSQLDB and later H2 and Apache Derby: lightweight SQL storage and test databases inside Java applications. Releases never got past 1.0 milestone builds (1.0-M1 and later -dev snapshots on Maven Central), development faded around 2007, and Tigris.org itself shut down in 2020.
statusNote: Development ended around 2007 at 1.0 milestone builds; Tigris.org hosting closed in 2020. Use H2, HSQLDB or Apache Derby.

scale.notes: In-process database for a single JVM.

strengths: Pure Java with a JDBC driver, so it embeds anywhere a JVM runs
Choice of in-memory or disk-backed tables
Snapshot-isolation transactions and B-tree indexes in a small footprint
weaknesses: Abandoned for nearly two decades; never reached a 1.0 final release
Original website and source repository are gone with Tigris.org
Far less SQL coverage and tooling than H2, HSQLDB or Derby
useCases: Maintaining old Java applications that bundle Axion
Studying early pure-Java SQL engine design
notIdealFor: New Java projects (use H2, HSQLDB or Apache Derby)
